elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date") and not all conditional automatic-renewal elements are satisfied (opt-out is 60 days, not ≤30; no Vendor reminder), so the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — a 12-month renewal term.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered text requires "sixty (60) days written notice" to avoid renewal; preferred ceiling is 30 days. Repair: change the Customer non-renewal notice to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder mechanic appears anywhere in Section 4.1 or the rendered language; Vendor owes no pre-renewal notice. Repair: insert an express obligation on Vendor to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 4.1 renews on existing terms and the Section 3.1 revenue-share (30% of Net Sales above the monthly threshold) contains no renewal uplift mechanic, so no price-increase right exists to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 replaces "ninety (90) days written notice" with "sixty (60) days written notice" in the automatic-renewal sentence; the rendered clause now reads "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon sixty (60) days written notice to the other" — exactly at the 60-day ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not triggered: the renewal continues on the existing revenue-share economics and no uplift, indexation, or list-price mechanic exists in the document, so there is no price increase to cap.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single numeric edit (90 → 60 days) brings the Customer non-renewal window to the 60-day ceiling, and the price-cap element is untriggered because the agreement contains no renewal price-increase mechanic.

Preferred is not complete: the 60-day opt-out exceeds the 30-day preferred ceiling and there is no Vendor pre-renewal reminder obligation. Both are preferred-level refinements, correctly noted rather than separately flagged.
The original 90-day window materially failed the fallback ceiling, so 'deviation' is the correct classification and a redline is warranted.

Minimality holds: one number changed inside the target sentence, defined terms (Effective Date, Termination Date) and the renewal term length, revenue-share economics, and notice-content sentence all survive untouched; no extras, survival tails, or procedures added.

Caution (not a failure): the amended notice period is bilateral, so shortening it also cuts the notice Vendor must give from 90 to 60 days, reducing Customer's runway against a Vendor exit. If preserving that protection matters, consider a party-specific formulation (e.g., termination/non-renewal by Customer on sixty (60) days' notice, by Vendor on ninety (90) days' notice) rather than a single shared figure.
Intent preserved: no dangling cross-references, undefined terms, or contradictory retained sentences; the Termination Date definition and the specify-the-date sentence continue to operate.
